text:
cassie: Quick async standup — what I did / blockers / today

cassie: What I did: looked into the late-night alert storm (04:12–04:20 UTC) for /generate endpoints. Found a spike in KV-cache misses and a small correlation with a canary rollout.
cassie: Blockers: runbook for cross-region redis failover is incomplete (missing the `promote-replica` step and the exact healthcheck thresholds). Also need a rereview for the debounce rule so we don't page on transient errors.
cassie: Today: patch a temporary debounce on the alert, follow up with a runbook PR, and coordinate a rollback if latency doesn't improve by 09:00 UTC.

omar: Noted SLO impact: 5m tail latency breached 2x the threshold during the spike, error budget usage +1.2%. Putting the grafana link here: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/SLOs/gen-latency
omar: Also saw increased token queueing on the dedicated fleet, likely caused by the canary config that reduces batching.

kevin: I'll take runbook PR. Can you paste the minimal repro steps/logs? I'll add the `promote-replica` snippet and a short rollback checklist.

cassie: Logs (relevant excerpt):
```
[04:13:05] warn kv: miss key=ctx:client-123 seq=1245
[04:13:06] error serve: request-queue-depth=312 route=/generate model=gpt-redwood-v2
[04:13:08] info autoscale: triggered scale_up count=2 target=gpu-pool-dedicated
```
cassie: Repro: run load test against canary (payload attached to thread), observe queue depth >300 within ~3m; KV miss rate goes from 0.8% -> 6%.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] 04:12 UTC — Route /generate p95 latency 1.8s (SLO 1.2s) — 27 occurrences. Pager: eng-sre oncall. Incident ID: INC-2026-0427-12

tay: Suggestion: apply a short 60s debounce on the route alert and add a rolling window check so we don't double-page on autoscale events. Also can we throttle canary traffic back to 10% while we triage?

kevin: Agreed on debounce. I'll open a small alertrules PR and a canary throttling toggle in infra-config. Tagging @tay for quick review.
kevin: PR will include the `promote-replica` command snippet and exact healthcheck thresholds.

cassie: Thanks — I can test the throttle on staging now and report results. If staging looks good I'll run the throttle in prod at :15.

sre-lead: Good catches. Please add an entry to weekly reliability retro with the timeline and the canary config diff. Also include cost impact of the autoscale bounce (estimate +$80 for the burst).
sre-lead: If this hits again, escalate to infra on-call and consider a temporary model-variant fallback.

kevin: Opening PRs and issue now: RB-#412 (runbook), AR-#89 (alert debounce). ETA for PR: 2 hours.

cassie: Update: staging throttle reduced canary to 8% and queue depth flattened to <80 after ~5m. Will monitor and push to prod throttle at :15 if stable.

cassie: tagging follow-ups — @kevin please assign RB-#412 to me for doc updates; @omar please add the SLO timeline to the incident notes.

omar: Will add timeline and slo-impact graphs.

kevin: Assigned and pinged reviewers. :thumbsup:

cassie: Thanks team — will post a short postmortem draft if prod stabilizes.
